articleTitle: Timing Analysis - A Necessary Improvement of EMI Emission Tests
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Minimizing the total measurement time is an important goal of automated emission measurements. The measurement times, respectively sweep times and test procedures have to take the signal characteristics into account. Special attention must be drawn to the proper detection and measurement of all kinds of disturbance: both continuous and intermittent narrowband as well as broadband disturbances. Time analysis will show the pulse repetition interval, pulse duration etc. for a proper setting of measurement times. The discussion is not restricted to fully automated measurements. In many cases, measurements need to be semiautomated, i.e. partially interactive and automated. Examples of timing analysis show why automated emission measurements cannnot be executed with one single test procedure.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of the Interferences Produced by ESD Via a Differential and an Integral Method
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Aim of this paper is to compare the features and the performances of an integral and a differential method for the numerical analysis of ESD problems. The integral method is deduced from the electrical charge density conservation law and from the Ohm’s law, expressed by means of the retarded potentials, and following a suitable decomposition of the conductive regions in elementary volumes. The differential method is deduced by the FDTD Yee-algorithm, where a suitable model of the ESD and a proper numerical treatment of the boundary conditions are made. A numerical analysis of a benchmark problem, constituted by an arrangement of a metallic enclosure stroked by ESD, cord and grid conductors, and grounding connections is performed, by means of the both methods. In addition this benchmark structure has been designed and realised and a comparison among the numerical predictions and the measurements made, is presented.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Crosstalk on a Multilayer Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility

authors.preferredName: P. C. T. van der Laan

abstract: In multilayer printed circuit board (PCB), a ground plane (GP) acts as return for the current through the tracks. The high-frequency (HF) coupling or crosstalk on a triple layer printed circuit board (PCB) was studied; the crosstalk was expressed in terms of a transfer impedance Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> between different circuits on the PCB. The continuous GP of our triple layer PCB was the middle layer; test tracks were placed at various positions and were of different complexity. Rapid HF calculations were carried out, based on transmission-line models. This avoids the use of time consuming three-dimensional calculations; the theory was checked by extensive measurements.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of Gaskets: The Influence of Mechanical Design Parameters
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to maintain a good conductive contact between different parts of a shielding box, and to maintain a good shielding value, conductive gaskets are used. This paper will focus on several mechanical design parameters influencing the shielding effectiveness of the resulting combination of shielding enclosure and applied gasket. For this case, it is understood that a good mating of materials is done, so that galvanic corrosion will not be discussed in this paper. It is shown that all parameters are not equally influencing the shielding effectiveness of the gasket/enclosure combination under different EM conditions: differences are noted for plane wave (far field) and magnetic near field conditions.

articleTitle: The Use of Signal Processing Algorithms in EMC
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Statistical signal processing is applied to estimate the geometrical and electrical characteristics of narrowband emissive sources. The key issue of the approach is based upon the use of MUSIC algorithm, which is largely used in array processing in far field conditions, to estimate the positions and the characteristics of emissive sources operating in near field conditions. The processing is divided in two phases : detection aimed to define the type of source and the estimation aimed to pinpoint the actual geometrical position of the source.

articleTitle: Aproach to Solving Problems of Electromagnetic Compatibility in HPP Peruća
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes an approach to solving the problems of electromagnetic compatibility in the hydropower plant Peruća, which is in the process of refurbishment Possible sources of electromagnetic disturbances are identified Coupling paths of electromagnetic disturbances and their influence on the sensitive electronic equipment are studied Special attention is paid to the metal enclosed SF6 switchgear 110 kV as one of the most powerful sources of electromagnetic disturbances. The paper gives proposition of measures for reducing electromagnetic disturbances. Measurements for finding out the level of electromagnetic compatibility in the complicated hydropower plant system, which contains both power and electronic equipment, are proposed This paper is a short presentation of a detailed study [1].

articleTitle: Simulations of Small Apertures and Grids by the FDTD Method
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Good screening practice requires all apertures in an enclosure to be electrically small. In this paper, a subcellular algorithm for the implementation of small apertures in the FDTD method is presented. The algorithm is based on the dipole approximation for a small aperture in an infinite screen. Using the concept of polarizability density, the algorithm can be extended to large arrays of apertures or grids. The algorithm is validated by comparison with measurements on a dedicated test enclosure.

articleTitle: Experimental Characterization of the Attenuation and Radiation Due to Bended Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The following paper deals with experimental results earned out in a reverberating chamber’s environment in order to estimate the electromagnetic emission of discontinuities in transmission lines.

articleTitle: Evaluation of SAR and Temperature Distribution in Subjects Exposed in the Far-Field of Radiating Radio Frequency Sources
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work a subject exposed to the far field of RF broadcasting sources has been considered. The incident field has been supposed to be a plane wave of variable frequency from 20 to 900. In a previous work, we have shown that in particular situations SAR evaluation could be not sufficient to establish if a given exposure is safe from a thermal point of view. In fact, heating is strongly influenced not only by the power dissipated in a certain volume of tissue and by the way in which absorption is distributed in the volume, but also by the thermal characteristics of the tissues and the heat exchanges. For this reason in this work we have solved both the electromagnetic and the thermal problem. In particular, the FDTD method has been used for computing the electromagnetic field distribution inside the exposed body, while an explicit finite difference formulation of the Bio-Heat equation has been adopted for computing the temperature increase. The obtained results have shown that thermal analysis gives a more complete information on the exposure hazard than SAR analysis alone.

articleTitle: Numerical Design of an Electron Ribbon Beam Gun of Pierce Type in Three Dimensions
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, an electron ribbon beam gun (Pierce type) is designed. The electrostatic force, including space charge density, is rigorously and fully treated in three dimensions (3D). To save computer memory storage and to reduce computing time an algorithm for calculating a space charge density is proposed. An adaptive control Runge Kutta method is used for beam rays tracing.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Wave Propagation in Superconductor-Dielectric Multilayers
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A theoretical study of electromagnetic wave propagation in multilayered structure composed of alternating insulator and thin type-Π superconductor films is presented A thin superconductor film is regarded as a boundary condition by force-induced fluxon movement. The dispersion relations for a p-polarized waves propagating in arbitrary directions in infinite superconductor-insulator superlattices under an external magnetic field applied perpendicular to the interfaces of the superlattice are calculated. The complex Bloch wave number is found. The imaginary part of the Bloch wave number can be equalled to zero for large speeds of fluxon movement. The reflection coefficient from multilayered structure insulator-superconductor with respect to the angle of incidence, external magnetic field and thickness of the superconductor layers is also calculated. The reflectance calculation shows that the coupling of electromagnetic wave to the flux-line-lattice in superconductor layers can increase the reflection coefficient significantly.

articleTitle: Time Domain Space Expansion Solution of the Nonuniform Multiconductor Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a new Time Domain Space Expansion (TDSE) simulation method for the Nonuniform Multiconductor Transmission Lines (NMTL). The method is based on a weak formulation obtained by expanding the voltages and currents along the line into some trial functions and projecting the NMTL equations through suitable test functions. This results in a discretized system of ODE’s which can be solved with a time integration routine. Different formulations of the TDSE method are presented and compared under the computational standpoint. The method is validated through several numerical examples.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Thick Dipole Antenna with End Disks for EMC Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The thick dipole antenna with end disks is studied to check the possibility of using it as the broadband antenna in EMC measurements. The input impedance and radiation pattern are obtained from the current distribution by solving an integral equation using the method of moments. The antenna factor and gain of this antenna are computed and compared with those of the biconical antenna. The comparisons of the computed results with measured data are made for the validity of analysis method.

articleTitle: A Method of Moments Solution of Scattering by Hydrometeors in Resonance Frequency Region
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of prediction of electromagnetic fields attenuation and scattering due to propagation through hydrometeors has been investigated. A new numerical method based on modal decomposition of volume integral equation together with the method-of-moments approach has been proposed. Careful verification procedure has been performed which included comparison with several examples of solutions to the problem of scattering by dielectric obstacles. Sample calculation results for scattering by rain particles are given.

articleTitle: EMC Related with Safe Design of Grounding System to be Formed by Pedestrian Metalic Sky Way and Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aim of this paper is to analyze the safe utilization by the people that uses a pedestrian metallic sky way in the city of Porto Alegre (State of Rio Grande do Sul - Brazil), situated under 230 kV and 69 kV transmission lines. The studies implemented were: (a) design of safe grounding system using the Finite Element Method in three dimensions (FEM - 3D) with representation of unbounded region by Infinite Elements (IE), (b) determination of induced currents generated by transmission lines and the knowledge of magnetic fields inside and around of the pedestrian metallic sky way. The studies shows that additional safe procedures need be done in grounding system and in the shielding of pedestrian metallic sky way.

articleTitle: Cross Polarization Test Results for the XCell and Compliance with Emerging Standards
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The subject of this paper is the analysis of a double polarization TEM transmission line device for radiated EMC measurements, the XCell. The main focus is on the evolving requirements of the radiated immunity standards for TEM cells, stating limits on the cross polarization level of the electric fields actually generated. These requirements are new to EMC applications, and considerably more stringent than those applied to anechoic chamber immunity testing. An experimental optimization for the XCell in the frequency range 80 MHz - 1 GHz has been performed. It is discussed in this paper together with experimental results for the field uniformity and cross polarization performance are shown. Despite the complexity of a double polarization device, low cross polarization levels have been obtained compliant with the present version of the new standard.

articleTitle: ELF Field Characterization of Electrical Energy Generation, Transmission and Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Concern about possible biological effects due to exposure to ELF fields produced by electrical energy generation, transmission, distribution and utilisation systems has led to the indication of exposure limits by national and international bodies. To verify the conditions of generation, transmission and distribution plants, with reference to the exposure of workers and general public, and to identify possible critical conditions with respect to the established limits, a measurement campaign has been carried out on the installations of the Azienda Energetica Metropolitana (AEM) of Torino. In the paper, the adopted measurement procedure and the measured electric and magnetic field values are reported and discussed as a function of the different analysed environments (generation plants, high voltage open air substations, distribution substations and tramway network supply substations) and compliance with exposure limits is analysed.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Power Frequency Magnetic Field Emission of Generator Busbar
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the magnetic field caused in the control room of a generating station by the operational current (rated value 3316 A) of a generator bus-bar is investigated at power frequency in steady-state case. The bus-bar system is installed just under of the control room (at 1.2 m below the floor) where the sensitive apparatus, including monitors, arc to be installed on the course of the scheduled renewal of the control and protection systems of that station. Firstly, the magnetic field strength in the environment of the busbar has been calculated by the 3D_FIELDS computer program and has been checked by site measurements applying mapping magnetic field recorder. Very high magnetic induction (ranging up to 260 μΤ) has been identified. Thus, it becomes evident that, the emission of magnetic field should be reduced by appropriate shielding of the busbar system. For this purpose the effectiveness of well conducting aluminium shielding structures of different constructions (busbars with different arrangement, rectangular cover, tubular cover) applied to each phase has been investigated. The effect of the bonding between the shielding of different phases has been analysed for different construction and lengths. To characterise the shielding effectiveness the resultant magnetic field has been evaluated on the bases of actual current distribution calculated by the CDEGS software package. The limitations in the application of a simple analytical calculation method has also be identified.

articleTitle: A Study of Magnetic Deflection System External Field as a Source of Noise
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The analysis of external magnetic field of a magnetic deflection systems, which are used in majority of cathode-ray tubes, is given. This field is considered as the noise relatively to the external units. The analysis includes the estimation of the field intensity space distribution, character of the field frequency spectrum, the effectiveness of deflection system magnetic shielding as the main means of noise decreasing.

articleTitle: Computational Investigation of Radiation from Conducting Boxes with Arbitrary Apertures
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The importance of obtaining relevant design information about a system before actually building a system is well known. In this work, an application of the electromagnetic simulation to obtain electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and interference (EMI) information during the design phase of electronic system enclosures is reported. For this purpose, full-wave electromagnetic characterization of various packages has been performed using a rigorous, accurate, and efficient electromagnetic analysis program. The computational technique is outlined in Section 2.

articleTitle: Improving the Field Homogeneity using a Mode-Stirred Chamber
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the usage of a Mode-Stirred Chamber for improving the field homogeneity of a shielded room. Simulations with a TLM-based time-domain computer program show an improved field uniformity in a plane which consists of 20 points. It will be shown how the field depends on the type of mode stirrers and of the positions. All results will be compared to a rectangular reference room without any stirrer or absorbing materials. The simulation result was evaluated by measurements in two real mode-stirred chambers.

articleTitle: Shielding Properties of a Conducting Cable Duct
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Subject of investigation is the shielding effectiveness of a conducting ferromagnetic cable duct which guides a bunch of exciting three-phase power cables. We solve the plane eddy current problem of the given system with the help of two corresponding boundary integral equations written for the vector potential and the tangential magnetic field strength. The integrals are evaluated numerically by applying the Gaussian method. To achieve high integration accuracy in close vicinity to singularities of the integrands we transform these integrands by the help of error-functions. The unknown functions on the surface of the cable duct are approximated in two different ways; numerically by using high order polynomials, and analytically by applying sets of orthogonal functions. As new analytical findings we publish integral representations for the Hankel functions H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup> and Η<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup> which act as kernels of the above integral equations.

articleTitle: Digital Radio System Range Reduction Due to Radiated Electromagnetic Interference
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Co-location between digital radio systems and electronic equipment can lead to severe interference problems. Unintentional radiated electromagnetic emission can increase the Bit Error Probability (BEP) in the digital radio receiver, and thus reduce the range of secure operation. The required increase in Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR), to compensate for this increase in BEP, is calculated for different separation distances between the undesired interference source and the digital radio receiver. This required increasement in SNR is also related to the corresponding reduction in operating range for the communication link. The calculations are performed for colocated electronic equpiment whose interference levels equals three radiated standard limits; EN 55022 Class A and Class B, and a typical military limit; RE 102 from MIL-STD-461 D. The digital radio system is assumed to use the modulation scheme Minimum Shift Keying (MSK). The results for an operating frequency at 60 MHz and 900 MHz, and BEP requirements of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> is compared. The conclusion is that RE 102 does not give any range reduction for separation distances greater than 10 m. The civilian radiated emission limits, however, give considerable range reductions at separation distances up to 40 - 50 meters and a required BEP of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, depending on what operating frequency is used by the digital radio system. At 60 MHz, at 10 m separation distance to the interference source, the Class B limit reduces the range with a factor 3, for a BEP of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>. The impact at 900 MHz is less than at 60 MHz. For a BEP of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>, the civilian radiated limits gives considerable range reductions at separation distances up to 50 - 60 m. The results shows that the interference from civilian electronic equpiment, co-located to digital radio receivers, must be thoroughly controlled to not affect the operating range of the radio system.

articleTitle: Quality Standards for Critical Application Software in Electromagnetic Pollution Environments
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The modem trend in quality is heading for the new concept of 'total quality' involving not only the single products in their specific fields, but also the producer and his methodology in producing. This means that the standardization should identify procedures, tests and validations schemes as generally as possible; this goal can be reached by generalizing test methodologies so as to produce rules for every field. Standards about software and hardware quality, especially for critical applications, do not at all guarantee reliability, safety and security of embedded hard real-time systems in electromagnetic pollution environments. In order to increase the dependability considerate as quality of the system a new design methodology is proposed. In this procedure a dependability program is introduced in which the EMC problems starting from the concept and definition phase should be considered. In this view the component hardware and software should be considered as a single unit: for them it is therefore possible to define the dependability functions and to determine the hardware-software integrity level in according with the EMC requirements. Once the dependability specifications for the hardware-software have been defined the design and develop phase is started and the joined and competing design (co-design) of the hardware-software is introduced. By this hardware-software view the validation tests are defined in which EMC factors are taken into account.

articleTitle: Geomagnetic Perturbances Caused by Underground Explosion
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The initial stage of geomagnetic variations (GMV) caused by underground nuclear explosion for arbitrary magnetic inclination is considered. We assume hot plasma ball magnetic moment as a triangular pulse in time. The spatial components of GMV electrical and magnetic fields as functions of time, epicentric distance, magnetic inclination and declination, ground conductivity and magnetic moment of source are calculated. Modelled signal shape is like to initial experimental record part (St. Nevada explosions 1988).

articleTitle: Computation of MTL Parameters by Means of a Finite Element Procedure
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a method is described for the finite element solution of skin effect problems in multiconductor transmission lines (MTL) embedded in an unbounded medium. The conductors may exhibit arbitrary cross-sections and electric and magnetic non-homogeneities. An integrodifferential equation in terms of the magnetic vector potential is employed in the formulation. A fictitious truncation boundary is introduced, on which the magnetic vector potential (Dirichlet boundary condition) is first guessed and then iteratively improved making use of the two-dimensional free-space Green’s function. The per-unit-length resistances and internal inductances are easily evaluated in post-processing. Examples are given in order to show the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Study of Chip Level Design for Attenuating Radiated EMI and Enhancing Set ESD Charateristics
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Overall EMC level of keyboard controlled IC has been improved to the level of satisfaction in the FCC specification, only by applying solutions in a chip level design. The ground-to-power line decoupling capacitor, the output RC filtering (or capacitor alone), the formation of microstrip line, and power line comer bending have shown to be possible solutions for supressing EMI characteritics at the chip level. The output RC filtering combined with ground-to-power line decoupling capacitor has resulted in suppressing radiated EMI the most. The electric field peak and average value were improved by 8.8dB and 3.1dB, repectively. On the other hand, Set ESD, which can be regraded as a kind of EMS, was also investigated for the same chip. The Set ESD immunity was found strongly dependent on power and ground fluctuation. Therefore, power line decoupling capacitor and the design optimization to maximize input noise margin at the output port latch have shown to be effective solutions to improve the Set ESD immunity.

articleTitle: Uncertainties Due to Cross-Polar Coupling in GTEM Cell Emission Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The OATS is the standard environment for emission measurements. Thus the GTEM cell data have to be correlated with the OATS results. Conventional methods to perform this correlation consider the equipment-under-test as a set of electric and magnetic dipole moments. These dipole moments are assumed to be in phase and phase information can not be obtained by GTEM cell measurements. Hence, cross-polar coupling in GTEM cell measurements leads to uncertainties in GTEM to OATS correlations. This paper presents a method to determine upper and lower limits for these uncertainties. It demonstrates the consequences of this effect on OATS predictions with GTEM cell measurement.

articleTitle: 3D FEM Analysis of Electromagnetic Wave Scattering from Conducting Wires and Dielectric Sheets in EMC Problems
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We propose in this paper an efficient method to study electromagnetic wave scattering by thin wires and sheets in 3D. The technique takes into account a conducting wire or a dielectric sheet of complex permittivity by using special finite elements so called « wire element » and « sheet element » respectively. The developed procedure is very convenient to implement in an edge element formulation. The theory and formulation of the finite element model is first described. Then, numerical computations are carried out to validate the method.

articleTitle: A Microwave Absorber Added with a Narrow Band Absorbing Property in the UHF Region
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Microwave absorbers added with a narrow band absorbing property in the UHF region is proposed. Three types of microwave absorbers, pyramidal, multilayers and zigzag carbon mat types, are backed with the plate formed-polystyrenes whose back surfaces are also pasted by sheets of carbon fiber mat. A remodeling design method of these microwave absorbers into the composite absorbers stated above is presented and several operating tests for three remodeled absorbers are also reported. Numerical discussions about a pyramid type is added. This composite absorber can be easily fabricated and be utilized for an effective remodeling the microwave anechoic chambers inexpensively.

articleTitle: Remote E-Field Sensor Without Cable Interconnection
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents first results in developing a remote sensor to detect fixed levels of electric fields without any cable connections. This sensor avoids field distortions due to power supply cable and/or signal transmission cable. If placed inside a metallic enclosure, this sensor does not need any break-out holes for signal transmission. The sensor is battery-powered and the signal from the remote sensor to a monitoring device is transmitted by low-frequency radiation. These features make the sensor particularly attractive for investigation of electric fields in TEM- and GTEM-cells but this device can be applied in non-closed configurations as well (e. g. open fields).

articleTitle: A Comparison of the at and BT Railway Systems from an Induction Point of View, using a Multiconductor Simulation
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the case of AC railway electrification with simple rail/earth return system, a significant part of the return (operational or short circuit) current is flowing through the earth. This kind of return current can induce high longitudinal voltages e.g. in a telecommunication cable laid in the vicinity of the railway line. This can be particularly significant when electrified railway routes pass through sparsely developed areas or the specific resistivity of the soil is high. For controlling the induced voltages in line-side metallic conductors, two special AC schemes, the booster transformer (BT) and the auto transformer (AT) systems, have been developed. In order to provide a basis for comparing the characteristics of these alternative schemes, computer simulations have been performed on a typical 30 km section of a single track railway using parameters based on the general practice. This paper provides a comparison between the effectiveness of BT and AT schemes in minimising the earth current. It also provides some basic comments on the voltage regulation of the two systems, the importance of the line balance, and the effect of the rail leakage conductance on the rail-to-earth potential.

articleTitle: Interference Environment for Protection and Control Equipment during Normal Operating Conditions Compared to IEC 1000-4-4
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Conducted electrical fast transients (EFT) which occur after switching of inductive loads (relay coils and contactors) is one of the most common and severe disturbances for protection and control equipment in high voltage stations. EFT's are also often the main cause of malfunction and deterioration of components in electronic equipment. This paper describes a study concerning measurements of conducted EFT's in nine high-voltage substations in order to map the electrical environment for protection and control during normal operating conditions. The results of the field measurements have been analysed statistically and compared to the results of measurements on two loaded burst generators complying with IEC 1000-4-4, in order to find out how the immunity test resembles the interferences in reality. A proposal, based upon the field measurement result, for a new standardized test voltage is also presented.

articleTitle: On the Use of Monopole Antenna Model in Lightning Protection System Analysis
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The current induced along a vertical metallic post and the buried horizontal wire is obtained by solving the corresponding homogeneous integro-differential equations. The excitation given in the form of lightning channel current is taken into account via the appropriate boundary conditions at the wires ends. The influence of a lossy half-space is taken into account by means of Sommerfeld integrals appearing in the integral equation kernel. These integral equations are solved by the finite element integral equation method, while Sommerfeld integrals are evaluated via the exponential approximation technique.

articleTitle: Effective Countermeasure for Common Mode Noise in Balanced Pair Lines with Common Mode Choke
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We have investigated an effective position of a common mode choke(CMC) to suppress a common mode noise for a capacitive unbalance along a balanced pair lines. We already derived a transmission parameter for the lines. In this paper, a transmission parameter which represents a CMC is derived as four-port network and LCTL(Longitudinal Conversion Transfer Loss; the measure of unbalance about earth) and distributions of both common mode voltage and current along the lines are calculated. As a result, we have shown that a CMC should be located after the unbalanced position on the lines to improve LCTL characteristic and a CMC must be inserted in the lines where we want to reduce a common mode noise current.

articleTitle: Ambiguity Function and Related Studies For Ultra Wideband Radar
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Recent development in high power sources and ultra fast switches made it possible to develop ultra wideband radars which have potential applications in surface and foliage penetration. detection of low radar cross section targets in clutter and also identification of target. This paper presents different ultra wideband waveforms. The generations of the waveforms arc based on Fourier series expansion of the desired waveforms. In order to investigate the potential of each waveform, the radar ambiguity function will be derived. The range - velocity resolution functions are obtained analytically and arc presented by a three - dimensional surface as a function of both time delay and Doppler time representing range and velocity. respectively.

articleTitle: Methods of Elimination of Frequency-Dependent Mutual Couplings in Models of Cable Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The calculation of transient in a time domain in a cable line system under the influence of the electromagnetic field with a defining spectrum of frequencies reaching hundreds megahertz calls for construction of equivalent circuits which take into account not only the frequency dependence of the own parameters of a cable, but also the frequency dependences of mutual couplings. Mutual frequency-dependent couplings cause the limitations in the choice of the method of transient calculation because they can’t be interpreted in the time domain. It must be Laplace or Fourier transformations or partial use of these methods in combination with the time domain methods. Methods of elimination of frequency-dependent mutual couplings in an equivalent circuit of a cable are offered. The use of the equivalent circuit of a cable without mutual couplings allows to calculate transients in the nonlinear circuits by a unified procedure in the time domain. The new equivalent circuit of a shielded radio-frequency cable is constructed. The results of transient calculation in a shielded cable loaded on a nonlinear overvoltage suppressor are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of Coupling Between Distributed-Constant Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Within the framework of coupled lines in the general theory of distributed-constant networks, a detailed case is presented relating to two lines which are structurally different in principle. The mathematical model thus obtained is examined numerically, with specific reference to compatibility and disturbances occurring between different lines. The study illustrated here is characterised by the systematic use of the concept of mutual wave impedance as an operator. The particular choice of working condition considered, in which the “slave” line is unloaded, demonstrates the Ferranti effect already known in the case of a single line.

articleTitle: The Use of an Active Test Board to Validate a Method That Predicts Differential Mode Radiated Emissions from Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The design of new Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) could be conveniently supported by the use of a fast and reliable estimations tool of the Radiated Emissions (RE). In this paper an active test board is used to validate a method aimed at predicting RE due to differential mode currents on PCB traces. The method takes into account effects of dielectric layer in the field calculation and does not need to discretise traces in short segments. It can simulate all traces of a PCB in a reasonable computation time. The simulation results are compared with measurements in a semi-anechoic chamber in far field. Radiation from the routed power net, on board batteries and batteries holders is put in evidence though measurement in near field. The paper shows the importance of modeling of components and of taking into account all couplings in the measurement set-up when comparing RE results. The method validated in this paper is included in the Telecom Hardware Robustness Inspection System (THRIS) for evaluation of telecom hardware.

articleTitle: Microwave Absorption Properties of M-Type Hexagonal Ferrites
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The microwave absorption properties of M-type hexagonal ferrites were investigated. The complex permeability and permittivity were measured using a network analyzer. articleTitle: Asymmetrical Noise Immunity Flip-Flop for the Use of Fail-Safe Component
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Generally, in digital circuit, it is uncertain whether its output changes to H or L for malfunction due to noise on power supply line. This makes difficult to design the fail-safe system of digital circuit in practical application. In this paper, asymmetrical noise immunity Flip-Flop whose noise immunity for noise on Vcc from H to L is different from it from L to H is proposed. It is shown that asymmetrical noise immunity characteristics can be intentionally realized by applying unbalanced ODF to two transistor which compose the Flip-Flop circuit, and design method to realize an asymmetrical noise immunity Flip-Flop is also shown.

articleTitle: ESD Response of Linear Systems using Only Scalar CW Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The goal of this paper is to state a procedure that allows to estimate the behaviour of a linear system excited by non-sinusoidal sources (for example ESD), making use of CW measurements of its transfer function amplitude by low cost scalar instrumentation. The method, based on the synthesis of the transfer function by means of proper elementary structures, is efficient, simple and gives an upper bound of the system response in the time domain. Numerical results are validated by measurements in several cases, where the response to an ESD is recovered for coupled PCB traces and enclosures with apertures.

articleTitle: On the Accuracy of Approximate Methods for Calculating ELF Shielding Effectiveness of Infinite Planar Shields
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The infinite planar metallic sheet is often used as a canonical geometry when considering the design of electromagnetic shields. Over the years, approximate solutions of this problem have been developed and used extensively [1]. The purpose of this paper is to study the accuracy of these techniques.

articleTitle: A New Measurement Method of Shielding Effectiveness
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new method for measuring the shielding effectiveness of a shielding material is proposed The apparatus consists of an enlarged diameter inner conductor with tapered ends fitting into sleeves at the ends to make connection with the inner pin of an N-type connector. The outer conductor has been expanded to the appropriate dimensions to maintain 50 Ohm impedance. Two outer conductors may be jointed with flanges which have a tongue along the one outer conductor and groove ring along the other outer conductor. Inner conductors consist of two parts having a convexity at the end of one inner conductor and having a concavity at the end of other inner conductor. The convexity of one inner conductor is inserted in the center of the concavity of other inna conductor to joint two inner conductors. Electrical connections are made via these contact between the groove and tongue of outer conductor and between convexity and concavity of the inna conductors. They allow to transmit the signal, whether sample exists or not. Because the sample is sandwiched between flanges on the outer conductor and between the inna conductors, the apparatus maintains good electrical contact between the sample and the inna and outer conductors. An amorphous magnetic film (CoZrTaNb) fomed on 7- µ m-thick polyamide film by sputtering methord was selected for use in this test method evaluation. Measurements of the shielding effectiveness were made for the frequency range from 0.3 MHz to 6 GHz with a network analyzer. The shielding effectiveness obtained using the proposed flanged coaxial apparatus show excellent reproduction.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Effect of Lead-Wires on Measurement of Surge Impedance of Transmission-Line Tower
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we describe the analytical results of a method for measuring the surge impedance of a transmission-line tower. We pay a particular attention to electromagnetic effect of the current traveling lead-wires on the tower-top potential essential to the measurement.

articleTitle: Procedure and Results of Spectral Efficiency Estimation of GSM System
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the procedure of spectral efficiency estimation of real GSM system in practice. Developed on its basis the experimental results of spectral efficiency estimation of two main GSM networks in Russia - “Mobile TeleSystems" (Moscow) and “North-West GSM” (St. Petersburg) are also presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Transient Electric Field in Gas Insulated Substations and Coupling with Secondary Cables
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the last years gas insulated substations (GIS) have found a broad range of applications in various countries, in particular inside densely populated cities. Switching operations in GIS are generating very fast travelling waves having 5 - 10 ns rise times which propagate outside the GIS enclosure. The coupling between the radiated electric field and low-voltage cables induces currents in cable sheaths. To improve the electromagnetic compatibility of electronic devices by proper shielding and correct cable routing, the estimation of the amplitude of these currents can be very useful. Modelling of GIS, calculation of the electric field radiated by the GIS enclosure and the coupling between this field and secondary cables are the main subject of this paper. The models have been created using three computer codes. First two codes are well known namely the Electromagnetic Transients Program (EMTP) and the Numerical Electromagnetic Code (NEC). The third code is a coupling code developed in our laboratory. The equivalent models of the GIS should be suitable for a wide frequency spectrum (from hundreds of kilohertz up to hundreds of megahertz). Measurements of different phenomena were performed in a 125 kV GIS of the Electrical Utilities of Lausanne. Verifications of simulation results with measurements are presented.

articleTitle: A Stable Digital Filter Design Method for Modelling Frequency Dependent Boundaries in TLM
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the design of a recursive digital filter for modelling frequency dependent boundary conditions in the TLM method. These boundaries may be used to model the frequency dependent reflection and transmission behaviour of materials such as composites, where an analytical solution is unavailable due to the complexity of the internal structure or a lack of data. Increasing use of composite materials in areas such as aircraft construction have emphasised the need for a modelling technique capable of predicting the frequency dependent behaviour of such materials. Particular applications for this method lie in the modelling of thin absorbers such as ferrites, where a frequency dependent reflection coefficient is required, and in the modelling of the shielding effectiveness of equipment enclosures, aircraft structures, etc. where the frequency dependent transmission behaviour is required. As an improvement to earlier filter design techniques used for this purpose, the technique employed here guarantees the stability of the filter used to simulate the material. Results are shown for the magnitude and phase of the frequency response obtained from the filter.

articleTitle: Investigation into the Effect of Conductor Geometry and Neutral Earthing Practices on LV Surges
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A simulation exercise where the effect of different conductor geometries (vertical, horizontal and aerial bundled conductor (ABC)) and the effect of different earthing practices (Single Point Earthing (SPE) and multiple point earthing or a Multiple Earthed Neutral (MEN)) - was initiated because of the large number of failures of energy dispensers (EDs) - electronic prepayment meters - due to lightning and other mains-borne transients. Both induced lightning surges and surges resulting from direct strikes to the MV and LV feeders were investigated. This paper describes the results of the investigation of the effect of the different neutral earthing practices on the LV ABC surge environment.

articleTitle: Calculation of Electromagnetic Fields from Arbitrary Conductors Configurations in Time-Domain Simulations
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents an elegant expression for calculating the resultant eletromagnetic field produced by a transient (or steady-state condition) on cable currents or transmission lines. By taking into consideration a line disposed arbitrarily in the cartesian coordinate system, using the Maxwell equations and applying magnetic potential vector, we come to the generalized expressions for the electric and magnetic fields as a function of current and position in the time domain. This expression is a generalization of the expression proposed by Christopoulos in [1]. The method has shown to be very useful in applications where lines are disposed in arbitrary manners and especially in systems in which various lines are interconnected, such as lightning protection systems (LPS) or a grounding system. The results obtained with such expressions are compared with other numerical methods. The results are obtained applying TLM (Transmission Line Modelling) method to obtain the current transient.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Wave Absorber for Quasi-Microwave Band Containing Carbonyl-Iron Particles Surface-Covered with Organic Molecules
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Polymer composites containing carbonyl-iron particles whose surfaces are covered with organic molecules — a silane coupling agent — were designed for an electromagnetic wave absorber for the quasi-microwave band (1-3 GHz). This coupling treatment changes the surface property of the particles from hydrophilic to lipophilic, strengthening the affinity between particle and polymer. The treatment simultaneously decreases the electrical conductivity on the surface of the particle and consequently the bulk of composite. These composites can thus contain a large volume (up to 59vol%) of the particles and consequently show high permeability and permittivity (7 and 45, respectively, at 2 GHz) without generating much conductivity. These magnetic and electrical conditions, i.e., high permeability and permittivity with low conductivity enable us to produce a wave absorber for the quasimicrowave band that is thinner (about 2 mm thick) than a conventional spinel-type ferrite absorber (about 7 mm thick).

articleTitle: Simulation of the Effects of Printed Circuit Board Layout on Current Flow and Emission
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A full field simulation technique based on the TLM method is applied to the prediction of differential- and common-mode currents in simple printed circuit boards. The same functional circuit is implemented using five different layouts to assess the impact of layout on current flows and electromagnetic emissions. It is shown that differential- and common-mode currents contribute differently to emission at different frequencies and common-mode currents depend strongly on circuit layout.

articleTitle: Pulsed Electric Current Dipole/Dipole Interference
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A time-domain analysis of electromagnetic, pulsed electric current dipole/dipole interference is presented. The emitting and suscepting dipoles may be either electric dipoles" (short segments of electric current carrying wire) or "magnetic dipoles" (small electric current carrying wire loops). Their mutual orientation is arbitrary. The coupling path is radiative in nature and consists of an unbounded homogeneous, isotropic, lossless medium. Illustrative examples, using standard EMC pulse shapes, are constructed with the aid of programs written for this purpose. The corresponding spectral diagrams are also presented.

articleTitle: Studies of Electromagnetic Interference from Electrosurgical Units
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problems of electromagnetic interference in hospitals have become more and more frequent since the number of electronic equipments installed in this environment has increased continuously. In surgery rooms, these problems are much more common, because in these places are located some devices wich are the most susceptible to EMI, like patient-connected devices, and others wich are the most harmful sources of EMI, like electrosurgical units and perfusion machines. These problems had or could have had life-threatening consequences for patients and medical staff thus justifying the need for studying this subject. The main goals of this work are: to quantify with special equipments (spectrum analyser, antenna and a Line Impedance Stabilization Network - LISN) the electromagnetic emissions (conducted and radiated) of an Electrosurgical Unit -ESU-, to verify if these emissions are in accordance with the Electromagnetic Compatibility -EMC-standards for medical devices and, based on this analysis, to propose a set of alternatives do reduce the EMI generated by Electrosurgical Units. The results of the measurements of the electromagnetic emissions from an ESU prove that its emissions are greater than the emissions thresholds imposed by the EMC standards for medical devices.

articleTitle: Perturbation Models of Lossy Multiconductor Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we propose an effective dynamic model for electrically-long low-loss multiconductor transmission lines. The model is based on a perturbation approach and takes into account frequency-dependent losses. It amounts to simple and accurate characteristic equations expressed in terms of closed form elementary functions. Such characteristics are easily implemented in many simulation schemes and lead to efficient and accurate transient simulations with little programming efforts.

articleTitle: Redetermination of MHD-EMP Amplitude Characteristics and Spatial Distribution on the Ground Surface
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The report presents the three-dimensional numerical model to calculate MHD-EMP parameters considering the real slope of the Earth magnetic field power lines and Hall currents. The model is based on the solution of Maxwell equations in low frequency approximation applying the generalized Ohm's law. Calculation results were compared to experimental data of magnetometric measurements at different ranges and directions from the burst epicenter. The effect of horizontal component of geomagnetic field and Hall currents on MHD-EMD parameters has been studied. It was defined that these two factors taken into account can cause significant transformation of spatial distribution in tangential electric field amplitudes on the earth surface in comparison with two-dimensional calculation and three-dimensional calculation excluding Hall currents.

articleTitle: A Novel Frequency Selective Electromagnetic Field Sensor
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new frequency selective field strength sensor (150 kHz - 1 GHz) is described with high dynamic range, measuring all Poynting vector quantities (E, H, phase). A block diagram, including the synthesizer and the double superhet conversion down to 0 - 150 kHz is given. The principle uses transmission line sensor heads and special baluns with superb common mode rejection. Sensitivity data is shown, demonstrating the sensor’s application between several 100 V/m and about several 10 dBµV/m. For the first time is now a sensor known for EMI emission as well as immunity measurements in one instrument. The prototype sensor is controlled by a fiber optic link and a power supply comprises a compressed air generator turbine.

articleTitle: Study of a Detection Device of Electromagnetic Field Penetration in Faraday Cages
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we interest to a detection device of electromagnetic quality of shielded enclosures and especially interior problem. We suppose empty cage and we choose geometrical optic to model wave propagation in Faraday cage. The interior field is very disturbed and it is necessary to detect an increase of average power of field. Then, we use an omnidirectional antennas array which gives average power in cage.

articleTitle: Complex Antenna Factor of a Receiving Dipole Antenna with Two Coaxial Feeders
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The complex antenna factor (CAF) is a useful characteristic of antennas for transient field measurements. In this report, a receiving dipole antenna with two coaxial feeders is investigated. The equation to calculate the CAF with the effective length and input impedance of the antenna element is presented. The calculated CAF is compared with that measured by the reference antenna method. The values of CAF obtained by the two methods are close except around the one-wavelength frequency.

articleTitle: New Finding Method of Radiated Emission Sources Utilizing CISPR Emission Measurement System
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: New emission sources finding method, which uses only amplitude data without phase, applying the discrete singularity method is proposed. The position estimation deviation Δd between the estimated and the given current positions is less than 0.2m and the amplitude estimation deviation Δj is less than 1.6 dB when spherical dipole antennas are used as ideal emission sources. Consequently, it is revealed that the finding method can be applied to find emission sources on equipment under test at CISPR emission measurement.

articleTitle: Information Extraction from the Radiation of VDUs by Pattern Recognition Methods
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work, the information which is captured from the radiated and conducted emissions from the computers’ video display units (VDU) is analyzed and recognized. The results are compared with the available literature. As a new approach, storage of the emanation data in the digital environment and reconstruction of the display contents by converting this data into the image format with a software are introduced and analyzed.

articleTitle: Effects of Electromagnetic Interferences of High Amplitude on FET - Differential Amplifier in the Frequency Range of 100 MHz - 1 GHz
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the spurious effects involved at the output port of operational amplifier disturbed by a sine-wave form signal occuring at high frequencies. The spurious effects considered in the paper concern the offset voltage and the demodulation. From the experimental point of vue it is shown that these phenomena are due to the behaviour of the first stage of the amplifier and specially due to the pair of differential JFET. Two mechanism will be considered : the leakage of high frequencies towards the supply ports and the unbalanced distortion.

articleTitle: Exposure to Cellular Phones and EEG Activity
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The influence of radio frequency (RF) fields generated by cellular phones (analogues and digital models) on the brain function of 19 volunteers was investigated using quantitative analysis of electroencephalogram (Q-EEG). Operating frequencies of the phones were 900 or 1800 MHz. Ten volunteers were male, age range 28 - 48 year (mean age 37.7±6.6) and nine were female, age range 32 - 57 year (mean age 46.6±9.0). Six EEG-recordings were made to each volunteer. One of the recordings was a sham exposure, while one of the phones was on the normal position but off. The duration of the real exposure was 20 minutes. The EEG was obtained when the volunteers were resting, eyes closed but awake. One phone caused statistically significant change in the absolute power in the delta band. However, no difference in the relative power in the same band was seen, and no changes with other similar phone models were observed. Thus, observed difference in the absolute power is probably caused by the statistical chance.

articleTitle: A Multimedia Tool for the Continuing Education in Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The European Directive 89/336/ECC has established that all apparatus containing electric and electronic components must fulfil the European Standards on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC). Thus, designers and technicians of the electronics industry need to be trained in the field of EMC. We present a project aimed at realising a multimedia product for continuing education in EMC. The project belongs to a programme of the European Union for the implementation of a vocational training policy. The realisation of this product contributes to the development of new learning techniques, easily accessible to anyone owing a PC and interested in the subject. It represents a new method of study for a subject so far only presented in conventional textbooks.

articleTitle: Estimation of Conducted Disturbances Characteristics of Electrical Discharges on Resistive Loads
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a simple general electrical discharges circuit model for electrical discharges simulation in overvoltaged air gaps. A macroscopic circuital method of simulation utilising the standard SPICE network simulator, based on a bidimensional non-linear impedances network has been proposed. The structure of the simulation framework is designed to take into account the electrode geometries in a straightforward way. A study of conducted current waveform for different electrode geometries on resistive loads has been done. The simulation results have been compared with experimental data obtained by implementing a measurement system for the conducted currents on resistive loads stroked by electrical discharges.

articleTitle: National Regulatory Requirements - The Challenge for Global Business
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The challenge for global operating companies is, how to comply with worldwide regulatory EMC requirements, by minimizing the costs and efforts, though complying with the local laws.

articleTitle: A Simple Model for Calculating Penetration of ELF Magnetic Fields Through Apertures in Planar Shields
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One critical feature of low frequency magnetic shields is that of shield continuity. A shield is often constructed of several pieces. It can be shown that the electrical and/or magnetic continuity of the shield at these junctions may have a significant impact on the effectiveness of the overall shield. It is very important to realize that the size of the gap need not be large for this to be the case. Further, wire connections at periodic locations along the shield may not be sufficient. Apertures cut in a shield may also influence shield performance. This will definitely be true if the aperture in the shield is oriented to cut the natural path of either magnetic flux or electric current in the shield.

articleTitle: Real Time Measurements of Electrostatic Discharges on Screened Twisted Pair Cables
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A signal is induced on the conductors when an ESD pulse propagates along the screen of a symmetrical data cable. The amplitude of the induced signal depends on the level of discharge, the screen termination, etc. These effects have been recorded experimentally by making real-time measurements. In the paper we will present the results and explain our observations in detail.

articleTitle: A New Type Tem Cell for Generating Standard EM Fields
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The authors propose a new type TEM cell which can not only provide high field uniformity and optimum size of uniform area but also easily change the polarization of fields such as the ITEM cell and the 6P-TEM cell. To find a 50 Ω model, NRM (Newton Raphson method) mixed with MM (moment method) was used. In this paper, the electric field distribution and field uniformity of the uniform area of the cell was analyzed by MM.

articleTitle: Fundamental Time Domain Analysis of Stratified Shielding Geometries
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We present a new approach to study electromagnetic wave transients in multiple layer shields in the time domain. New analytical solutions of Maxwell’s equations modeling the wave propagation for arbitrary waveform functions in conductive media are applied. This provides new insights into physics of shielding by distinguishing between main wave parts and diffusive wave parts. Without loss of accuracy the method allows semi-numerical results even for Dirac-shaped pulses within a coarse grid. We derive impulse responses and demonstrate transient field computation via convolution. A time domain propagation model allows the explanation of waveform dispersion in conductive media.

articleTitle: Wavelet Transform Approach for Transmission Line Analysis
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new approach for the solution of transmission line problems is presented in this paper. The representation of differential and integral operators by wavelets on the interval is used to reduce the differential equations of multiconductor transmission lines in algebraic equations. Indeed, the solution is obtained by means of an algebraic system that gives the coefficients of the wavelet basis functions. Then, the solution is obtained avoiding time convolution, FFT and time stepping as in the conventional numerical methods. The performances of the method are tested considering uniform and nonuniform lines, and nonlinear loads.

articleTitle: RF Disturbance Field Produced by the Pantograph-Catenary Contact
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The current collection in high speed trains is a very important problem for the need of assuring a good electrical contact between the overhead line and the pantograph and for the radio frequency interference that such contact can generate. To reduce such interference, a controlled pantograph is under study within the frame of the “Progetto Finalizzato Trasporti” of the National Research Council (CNR) in Italy. In order to verify the influence on the radio frequency emission of some parameters, an apparatus simulating the pantograph contact has been built at the IEN laboratory. By means of a measuring system, equipped with a suitable antenna, the electromagnetic field radiated by the apparatus in the frequency range from 100 kHz to 1 GHz was recorded for different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Determination of EMC Degree Based on Probability Models of Microelectronic Systems Ensuring Railway Traffic Safety
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper is devoted to a novel method of application of probability models and their practical application as they are specified in IEC 61000-401 for determining the EMC of microelectronic safety devices. It is proposed to use a numerical measure of the failure probability employing a EMC par package for the Windows environment which allows to determine the required parameters of the electromagnetic environment and the degree of noise immunity for specified EMC levels. The method is more flexible compared with the existing “determinant” methods since it takes into account the probabilistic nature as a measure of noise levels and the degree of noise immunity allowing to express the EMC level numerically.

articleTitle: Field Uniformity Measurements in a Tem Cell using the Modulated Scattering Technique
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The use of the Modulated Scattering Technique (MST) to evaluate the intensity field distribution in a TEM (or GTEM) cell volume is proposed. If compared with the conventional ones, modulated Scattering probes, due to their limited size, may be very useful for probing field uniformity in the cell volume without introducing great perturbations in the electromagnetic field distribution under measurement. Besides MST measurements may be performed without no additional RF connection, but only employing the RF ports of the TEM cell.

articleTitle: Design of Interface Circuits for Industrial Process Control
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The correct design of the I/O-ports used in industrial process control is very important. The susceptibility against conducted interference without the use of expensive filtering and shielded interconnection lines is possible if the design of the circuits is adequate to the properties of the disturbances. In this paper suitable precautions for analog and digital circuits are described and realized interfaces are presented. The use of simulation during the design process is shown. Models for ESD, Burst and Surge generators are presented. The behaviour of the generators and tested circuits in the simulation is compared with measurements.

articleTitle: On Accuracy of Numerical EMC/EMI Modeling Over a Wide Frequency Range
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Numerical EMC/EMI modeling over a wide frequency range requires for an appropriate sampling scheme. Limited computer resources give rise to the strong limitation on the number of samples, especially during analysis of a complex system. A simple method for estimation of the sampling accuracy and the required number of samples is given. A technique for improving of the modeling computational efficiency is proposed.

articleTitle: Improved Design of Power Transmission Line Grounding Arrangements for Better Protection against Effects of Lightning
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Power transmission line grounding are usually assumed as concentrated grounding systems. Dynamic behavior of such grounding systems is usually analyzed taking into account only the soil ionization effects. In such cases the propagation effects are usually neglected. Also usually the design requirements for power transmission line grounding are based only on its commercial frequency resistance. This paper considers improved design of power transmission line grounding for better transient performance when they are subjected to fast fronted currents. In such cases propagation effects are dominant in the early time, even in the cases of grounding systems that are usually assumed as concentrated.

articleTitle: A Simple Formula for the Calculation of Peak Values of Currents Induced in Overhead Lines by Indirect Lightning Strokes. Theory and Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic field due to lightning strokes propagates at grazing angles, if, as it is generally assumed, the lightning channel is considered as a straight vertical antenna. Calculations have shown that, while the current or voltage peak value induced on the line, is practically proportional to the distance to the striking point and to the lightning current amplitude, the order of magnitude remains the same when the lightning striking point with respect to the line changes with the azimuth. The paper proposes a theoretical model for the peak value computation of the current induced by an electromagnetic plane wave, with the Poynting vector parallel to the line, that illuminates an overhead transmission line. This represents a good guess for the amplitude of currents and voltages induced by strikes at any other positions. Different configurations are analyzed. The results given by the proposed model are compared to experimental results and to other theoretical models. This simple approach can be used for rapid estimation of lightning indirect effects on overhead lines in a maximizing analysis.

articleTitle: Comparison Between Different Testing Methods Used in Electromagnetic Compatibility for Immunity Testing and Radiation Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Different testing methods are in use to study the behaviour of electronic equipment i.e. their immunity testing and emission measurements, by placing them in electro-magnetic environment. The methods under consideration are:

articleTitle: EM Field in Vicinity of Transmitting Mast Antennas on a Conducting Half-Space
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The structure of EM field and intensity of equivalent Pointing’s vector in vicinity of transmitting mast antennas placed on a conducting half-space are determined in this paper. Using the mathematical model of vertical antennas above the real earth, which has been developed by authors in their previous papers (EMC’96, J. AEÜ’97, COMPUMAG’97), the unknown current distributions (UCDs) and input impedance were calculated first. After that, the structure of EM field in vicinity of the antennas is determined using the definition expressions. The influence of the finite ground conductivity on the structure and strength of electric and magnetic field in vicinity of these antennas has been analyzed by numerical experiments presented in the form of the universal diagrams. The results for electric and magnetic field and intensity of equivalent Pointing’s vector are compared with the ones obtained when the real earth is treated as a perfect conducting medium.

articleTitle: Analysis of Microstrip Open-End and GAP Discontinuities by an Ameliorated Moments Method
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work, we cany out a full wave study of the Gap and Open-end discontinuities, using the ameliorated moment method proposed by Sonny & al. [9] which eliminate the spurious solutions in calculation of eigenmodes. A rigorous solution, for the radiation and the surface wave generation at high frequencies, is obtained and certain ameliorations are performed The results are given for the magnitude of reflection and transmission coefficients, the terminal and the coupling conductances and capacitances and for the excess length, versus the frequency and the substrate thickness for different values of the substrate permittivity and the microstrip width. Our results, given in form of curves, are compared to other results obtained by the quasistatic and the different full wave approaches and to experimental results.

articleTitle: Indirect Lightning Effects on Short Overhead Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aim of this paper is to quantify the lightning-induced disturbances on short overhead lines. An experimental study was carried out in Camp Blanding in 1995 in which the current induced on a short structure by artificially-initiated lightning was measured. For the considered electrically-short structures, is that the induced signals can be predicted with reasonable accuracy using a simple quasistatic approach. Further experiences conducted in a high voltage laboratory allowed us to propose protective solutions.

articleTitle: Practical Approach for Measuring Disturbed Signals in Frequency and Time Domain During Immunity Testing
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In automotive and many other industrial applications safety is of great concern. The safety of these applications is not only covered by the machine directive but also incorporated in strong immunity requirements. These strong immunity requirements will minimise the risk of an accidental failure due to disturbance by electromagnetic energy. This paper describes a method that will help the designer to investigate the designs by method of computer simulations and by getting measured data dining immunity testing. These data will give the engineer more information than just a pass/fail result. The computer model must be seen as a first approach model that describes the cable as a TL and the stripline - on which the immunity tests are based - as a large coupling capacitor. A resistor in a first step simulates the wire terminations. In a second simulation step, is the resistor replaced by for example a typical input circuit.

articleTitle: Measurement of Very Fast Voltage Rising Part Due to Micro GAP Discharge in Air
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Very fast voltage rise curves and fall curves due to gap discharge were considered in time domain. The measurement system consists of a distributed constant line system and a coaxial electrode, because the voltage transients are very rapid and fluctuations are complicated Semi-rigid coaxial cables were used as distributed constant lines. The coaxial electrode has matched impedance for a characteristic impedance of the semi-rigid coaxial cables. The atmosphere around the coaxial electrode is normal air. This distributed constant line experimental system enables to measure the high speed and high voltage transients of about 100 ps. As a consequence of the experiment using this measurement system, the voltage rise time was slown down from about 250 ps to about 350 ps due to increasing of source voltage from 800 V to 1400 V in positive polarity. The voltage fall time was slown down from about 250 ps to about 600 ps due to increasing of source voltage from 800 V to 1400 V in negative polarity.

articleTitle: Lightning Transient Response of 400 kV Transmission Tower with Associated Grounding System
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Tall structures such as transmission line towers, buildings and communication towers. are frequently exposed to lightning strikes. A field theory method is used in this paper to examine the transient behaviour of a lightning strike on a process in transmission tower structure and associated grounding system.
