A 39 m transmission tower connected to two different grounding grids is studied. Injecting a 20 kA current surge having a double exponential pulse waveshape simulates the lightning strike that energises the conductor network. The transient electromagnetic fields near the base of the tower are computed and plotted. The current distribution in the tower and associated grounding system, the scalar potential and the electric and magnetic fields are obtained using the HIFREQ module from the CDEGS (Current Distribution, Electromagnetic Fields, Grounding and Soil Structure Analysis) software package.

articleTitle: Fast Evaluation of the Susceptability and Emittivity of Shields with Rectangular Apertures
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of metal shields with apertures is a typical problem of electromagnetic compatibility. The apertures, generally present to allow cooling, air conditioning, cable connections and weight reduction, compromise the shielding electrical effectiveness. They general affect both the susceptability and the emittivity properties of the shielded body. As well known, the numerical analysis of apertures on a metal flange is a hard computing task. Therefore, in order to ensure affordable computing times, it is of paramount importance to select efficient numerical methods to simulate the behaviour of the single aperture, so that high efficiency is achieved also on multi-aperture problems. In this study, the problem of an efficient simulation of the radiating properties of a single rectangular aperture on a metal flange is addressed and solved. Three methods are implemented and compared, so that an optimum trade off among numerical accuracy, performance and robustness is found out. Among the three proposed methods, the one using a field expansion over the aperture with waveguide modes, as well as a transformation into the spectral domain, has proven to be the most attractive, since it can significantly reduce the computer times.

articleTitle: Technical Power Quality in Argentina’s Electricity Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The National Electricity Regulatory Agency {Ente Nacional Regulador de la Electricidad\ ENRE) has passed regulations [1] and [2], where distribution network electromagnetic compatibility levels are established. These rules supplement the legislation in force with respect to the quality of the technical product, establishing certain limits for harmonics and flicker values. The scope and some of the results arising from the application of these regulations, dealing with one of the three power supply controlling factors, are analyzed in this work.

articleTitle: A Simulation Model to Predict EM Radiated Interference with Control Equipment in Electric Power Distribution Substations during Switching Operations
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In electric power MV/LV substations, circuit-breakers have to be taken into account as EMI sources during switching operations. This paper deals with a simulation numerical model to predict electromagnetic interference with control equipment and electronic circuitry. A simulation example by applying the proposed model is carried out in order to show the flexibility of the computational tool. Transient electric and magnetic fields during switching operations are computed.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Shielding Effectiveness of a Real Enclosure
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We determine the shielding effectiveness (SE) of a real enclosure: a commercial, shielded 19" rack, with a complicated structure. We use simple, equivalent circuits to approximate the SE of multiple apertures and grids. To assess the SE of a complex shield, we first identify all possible points of leakage and simulate the belonging SE with the above simple and quick analysis method. By comparing and ranking the results, we are able to locate the most critical parts of the shield and to determine the total SE. A good agreement with measured results is obtained.

articleTitle: The Cisoid Concept and the Hertzian Potential in the Study of Radiated Disturbances
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Recalling the classical theory of the Hertzian dipole, its direct normalisation employing the operator method is proposed. After expressing the latter in the traditional sinusoidal form, it is then expanded into the more general cisoidal form which includes the presence of dissipative phenomena. The employment of the Hertzian potential finally permits the shortening of the logical process, which is presented in a form particularly well suited to its direct application to EMC engineering problems. Some numerical examples referring to applications in the traction field show that the approach fulfils all expectations.

articleTitle: Case Study of a Second-Generation, Real-Time, Remotely-Controlled Spectrum Monitoring System
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Canadian administration identified, in 1992, a need for monitoring facilities that are accessible from the field offices in the major population centres across Canada to assist in the resolution of radio interference problems and to gather data on the quality of the radio spectrum. Field offices are typically located in the downtown area of major urban centres. The location of these offices makes them poor sites for radio spectrum monitoring, hence the need for a capability of remoting the monitoring facilities to more suitable monitoring sites. To meet this challenge the Canadian administration has developed the INTEGRATED SPECTRUM OBSERVATION CENTRE (ISOC) system.

articleTitle: A Versatile Time Domain Integral Equation : Application to an Extension of the Theory of Lines and to an Integral Equation/FDTD Coupling
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with an original versatile time domain integral equation especially developed for being coupled with other theoretical approaches. Such hybrid approaches are well suited for the study of electromagnetic wave coupling with complex structures. Two kinds of applications will illustrate our aim : the first one will consist in the theoretical study of transient pulses propagation on long lines ; the theory of lines is extended to include radiation phenomena. The second one will show how to take oblique wires into account in FDTD grid thanks to a coupling with our integral equation.

articleTitle: An Effective Layer Model for Analyzing Fiber Composites
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we present expressions for the effective material properties of fiber composites that are commonly used in aircraft and EMC/EMI shielding materials. These expressions can be used to calculate efficiently the reflection and transmission coefficients and the shielding effectiveness of these fiber composites. We compare results of the reflection coefficient and shielding effectiveness obtained from these effective properties to results obtained from a finite-element (FE) solution of the actual periodic fiber composite. This comparison indicates that the model presented here is accurate - for representing the properties of fiber composites.

articleTitle: Effects of a Strong ELF Electric Field on the Human Electroencephalogram
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This investigation studied the effects of 50 Hz electric fields on the human brain. We developed a telemetry technique to measure the human electroencephalograms ( EEGs ) even in a strong Extremely Low Frequency ( ELF; 50 - 60 Hz ) electric field at an alternating high potential. With applying the telemetry system to the experiments, the EEGs were measured from nine subjects who exposed to a strong ELF electric field. The measured EEGs were analyzed by FFT. The integrated powers of δ, θ, α and β wave bands and the fluctuations of a waves were calculated from the spectral power densities of EEGs. Changes in the amplitude ( power densities of [δ] + [θ] + [α] ) of the EEGs that was one of the indexes of the vigilance level were observed.

articleTitle: A Simple Formula for the Dimensioning of the Model of Transmission Lines Exposed to External Fields
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The influence of external electromagnetic fields on transmission lines is most commonly modelled as lumped current and voltage sources distributed along the lines and at the line terminations while the lines themselves can be arbitrarily modelled. For the determination of the number of sources needed for the simulation, one has to find a trade-off of accuracy of the simulation results and the computing costs needed to obtain them. In this paper, for practical use, we present a simple formula for the estimation of the number of sources required for the simulation to obtain a solution within a certain error bound. Herein, the external field distribution, the frequency, and the line geometry are taken into account.

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of the Electromagnetic Field in Shielded Enclosure Configuration by the Mixed FD/WE-TD Method
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The mixed finite difference/Whitney elements time domain (FD/WE-TD) method is applied to the analysis of transient electromagnetic field in complex configurations such as enclosure with aperture. The mixed FD/WE-TD method consists in discretizing the region in two parts composed respectively by structured and unstructured elements and leads to an explicitimplicit solution scheme. In the structured mesh Yee's algorithm is applied to solve Maxwell's curl equations while in the unstructured mesh the Whitney elements-time domain method is applied to solve the wave equation. The method is very powerful since it permits to overcome some of the main limitations of the basic FDTD method, such as staircase in modelling of curved boundaries and uniform space discretization, without a significant increase of the computational cost. The procedure is tested in canonical configurations and then applied to the analysis of the electromagnetic field in shielded enclosure with aperture configurations.

articleTitle: Desensitization Reciprocal Mixing Effects : Analysis, Computation and Mitigation Techniques
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In modem radio systems the continious improvements in equipment have significantly reduced the effects of receiver (Rx) internal noise and improve its sensitivity. However, the present exponential increase in radio systems, users and equipments has tremendously enhanced the risk of intra- and intersystem Radio Frequency Interference (RFI). This paper investigates the main desensitization intrasystem RFI effects from the operation of worst case collocated transceivers. Semi-empirical computation methods are developed for the main effects of desensitization: 1. Preamplifier blocking or loss of sensitivity due to saturation was treated previously [1, 2, 3]. 2. The reciprocal mixing desensitization effect becomes dominant for HF and novel digital systems Rx where the input signals are usually applied to a frequency converter stage proceeding the pre amplifier stage. An extended qualitative analysis of reciprocal mixing is presented. Semi-empirical computation method is developed as well as a discussion on efficient mitigation methods to reduce the disturbing effects of reciprocal mixing and quantitative results are provided as function of the desensitization level for a typical high frequency scenario. The efficient mitigation methods can be applied in Rx for different frequency ranges and modulation methods.

articleTitle: Coupling Effects among Aerial Structures and Earthed Electrodes in a Lightning Protection System
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper proposes a field-approach global model suitable for simultaneously evaluate electromagnetic contributions and mutual influences of all the elements of a lightning protection system (LPS). Simulation case studies of realistic LPS are illustrated.

articleTitle: Protection of Wire-Line Communication Installations in the High-Voltage Substations Zone of Influence in Urban Areas
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The ground potential rise around high voltage substations, in case of ground faults, may cause dangerous voltages between telephone subscriber lines and local ground. A computer model of the substation grounding system and all connected uncoated metallic sheathed cables is used for estimation of the ground potential rise zone of influence on the subscription telecommunication installations in urban environment. The effect of the equalizing of potentials by other buried metallic networks, typical for the urban environment, is included in the model based on measured potentials in a small number of specified points.

articleTitle: Microwave Propagation Characteristics and Performances of Wireless Communication for Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Indoor electromagnetic environment needs to be controlled using building materials so that the wireless communication systems are designed effectively. We investigated experimentally and analytically the propagation characteristics at the 2.4-GHz ISM band for several indoor environments by using an electromagnetic environment evaluation booth where the ceiling, wall, and floor materials could be easily changed. The throughput and BER of a 2.4-GHz ISM band wireless LAN system were measured, and the results showed that reflections from the side walls cause a serious interference problem and the wireless LAN could not communicate at over 30% of its positions when the walls were made of high-reflection-coefficient materials. Our findings will be useful for designing indoor wireless communication systems that operate in the 2.4-GHz ISM band and at other frequencies widely used for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Statistical Characterisation of Electromagnetic Disturbances Produced by the Sparks between Pantograph and Catenary of TGV on a GSM Antenna
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to characterise the electromagnetic environment and the disturbances induced on a GSM antenna by the sparks between pantograph of the engine and catenary, two measurement campaigns were carried out on the german MORANE site at a maximal speed of 220 km/h and in France on different TGV lines at commercial speeds between 250 and 300 km/h. The paper presents the results obtained during the TGV measurement campaign in terms of waveform analysis, statistical analysis in the time and frequency domains, and a comparison of the results between the two campaigns.

articleTitle: The Requirements of a Uniform Field Distribution for Radiated Immunity: A Critical Analysis
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The European Standard EN 61000-4-3, giving a test method for EMC testing against radiated RF fields, is defining a type of uniform field distribution to be used. It describes a calibration of the test setup, looking for the field strength at 16 points, equally distributed over a surface area of 1.5 x 1.5 m. When 12 points are within a 0-6 dB distribution margin, the field is defined to have a uniform field distribution. In this paper, a critical analysis will be done on this requirement: on an open site, the field distribution has been recorded at two different distances from the transitting antenna (I and 3 m), at several frequencies. Two methods has been use for determining the uniformity of the field distribution, and they wil be compared, showing that in practice the requirement is not so severe. The measurements on open site are also compared with a test in a shielded room, just using a partial absorbing lining. Finally, a critical analysis will be given on the requirement with respect to the testing of small equipment, and of very large (industrial) machines.

articleTitle: Calculation and Measurement of the Shielding Effectiveness of Real Metallic Structures in Frequency and Time Domain
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Several kinds of electromagnetic field stresses can occur in very different places of the environment. The screening of electronic components against these electromagnetic fields due to housings or other metallic structures is therefore very important for EMC purposes: Electromagnetic transients produced by switching operations in HV-GIS (gasinsulated switchgear) have a broadband characteristic with frequencies up to 1 GHz [4]. The magnitudes of both the electric and the magnetic fields in HV-substations can reach high values [4]. This can cause a malfunction of the substation control equipment.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic and Mechanical Performances of a New Multilayer Composite Material
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Three new composite absorbing-structural materials are designed, realized and tested, considering both electromagnetic and mechanical requirements. They are sandwich structures composed of four layers, which are characterized by reflection coefficient lower than -17 dB from 8 GHZ to 18 GHz, and strength-to-weight ratio higher than aluminum.

articleTitle: Simulation of Non-Linear Protection Device using TLM Method
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A simulation technique based on the Transmission-Line Modelling Method (TLM) is applied to predict the behaviour of a transmission line, loaded by a resistor and protected by a non-linear device, called varistor. This application is normally used to protect electronic systems against conducted electromagnetic discharge. The excitation used to simulate the discharge is a high and fast square pulse and it is shown that the non-linear device reduce the value of the pulse on a resistive load. The main response of this time domain simulation is the voltage on the load and the measurement of the real response in a practical circuit was obtained to compare the results.

articleTitle: Application of Evolutionary Algorithms for Modeling of Conductors and Packages with Arbitrary Geometry
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In some applications, in particular EMC applications, it is necessary to model conducting structures such as wires, packages and interconnects. While it is possible to use analytic formulas for well defined geometries such as coaxial lines, this is not the case for complex arbitrary geometries. This paper suggests a solution of this problem based on evolutionary and genetic algorithms.

articleTitle: Research Activity About Environmental Low Frequency Magnetic Fields: Measurements in Case of Non Sinusoidal Source
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with a point of the research activity of our group about the prediction and the control of the levels of the low frequency magnetic field in the environment. The paper describes the coil probes we have realised for the measurement of the magnetic induction and the related calibration technique. The calibration is made either in amplitude or in frequency for an assigned magnetic configuration, and by means of the known distribution of the magnetic field, calculated with accuracy with classical numerical methods. The knowledge of the response in frequency of the probes allows an efficient reconstruction of the magnetic field wave in case of non sinusoidal source, when the use of a commercial field meter may be critical. The comparison of the computed values of the magnetic induction with the measurements made either by means of the proposed technique orby a commercial field meter shows that the measurement technique we use is efficient and in general more accurate than the use of field-meters commercially available.

articleTitle: Coupled Horizontal Dipole Antennas Above a Conducting Half-Space
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The unknown current distributions (UCDs), self and mutual impedances/admittances of coupled horizontal dipoles (CHD) with common equatorial plane (x0z plane), placed above a real earth, are determined in this paper. The UCDs are determined by numerical solving of system of integral equations of Hallen’s type (SIE-H) using a polynomial approximation for currents. The simplified expressions for potentials (Hertz vector potential and electric scalar potential), obtained with assumption that the module of refractive index ground/air is much greater than one, n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> >> 1, are used for establishing the SIE-H. Thus, the problem of numerical calculation of so-called Sommerfeld’s integrals is partially omitted. The paper shows that very accurate results for the current distributions and impedances of the antennas are obtained if n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> > 3. Fortunately, this condition is satisfied in most of the practical cases.

articleTitle: The Future of EMC Education: Keeping Faculty up to Date
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A unique opportunity has been given to faculty from engineering educations in Denmark. The Ministry of Education has funded networking of faculty with the objective to initiate a professional development in order to strengthen and renew the educations. This paper is an account of, how this opportunity was utilized to its frill extend by lecturers of EMC. The activities cover a so broad range, that the experience gained might be useful for colleagues working on similar projects.

articleTitle: Prediction of the Electromagnetic Pollution Due to AC Railway Systems. Influence of Traction Load Variability
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The magnetic field due to the high speed railway system is predicted. The real geometrical configuration and the time evolution of the currents in the conductors is taken into account, considering various traffic conditions. The procedure allows the duration curves of the magnetic flux density be determined, as essential information for long term human exposure studies.

articleTitle: Non-Thermal Radio Frequency Exposure of Humans, Animals and Other Biological Objects
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to examine effects of electromagnetic fields on biological systems, investigations on humans, animals and other biological materials like cells or cell-membranes have to be performed. This contribution reports on the development of exposure setups for these investigations and gives concrete examples of two recently designed exposure devices for experiments with humans and animals.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Mom-FDTD Technique for the Solution of EMC Problems
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new hybrid technique is presented to solve typical radiation problems in EMC, combining a marching on in time version of the Method of Moment (MoM) and the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method. The use of the equivalence principle with a proper set of fictitious sources allows to divide a complex radiation problem into two simpler problems, accounting for the coupling between actual sources and scatterers. The hybrid technique is first validated by means of preliminary tests and then applied to solve a problem of radiation through a slotted shield.

articleTitle: The EMC Implications of Low Voltage Directive Requirements
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: With the introduction of Low Voltage Directive 93/68/EEC and EMC Directive 89/336/EEC many times the manufacturers of electrical and electronic equipment are faced with contradictory requirements when they try to comply with applicable specifications related to both Directives. As everybody knows the Low Voltage Directive addresses human and product safety issues while the EMC Directive addresses electromagnetic environment pollution one. The point of contact is represented by grounding and bonding requirements, which are interpreted in different manners by the specifications of the two Directives. The aim of this paper is to try to clarify the implications involved in their implementation at both design and test level.

articleTitle: Contribution of the on Chip Power Supply Partitioning to the EMC System Performances
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The surrounding electromagnetic field generated by electronic equipment is due to the high frequency currents circulating through the cables and component interconnections. Each wire segment or current loop on the PCB, powered by these currents, behaves        like an antenna and radiates spurious electromagnetic fields. The currents responsible for these phenomena have a very large number of frequency harmonics. They are generated by the fast signal transitions inside high density, high speed Integrated Circuits. The purpose of this paper is to show, through a real case analysis, how power supply isolation between different logic blocks on a die, in certain conditions, may have a degrading impact on the final EMC performances. It represents the complete study which was carried out on a problematic device. This device was found to be noisy in the final application, thus preventing the application from successfully passing the final acceptance test. The first part of this paper describes a list of potential root causes, deduced from a preliminary analysis done on the module partitioning of the device and on the power supply routing (Vdd,Vss layout).. The second part presents the methodology which was used to perform the tests and measurements. This was done to confirm and evaluate the die layout and partitioning impact on the final EMC performances of the application.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of Wiring Cables with Improved Screening Applied in High Voltage Substation Environment
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to demonstrate the shielding effectiveness of the improved signalling cable the paper presents, firstly, the design of the screening of a cable and the results of laboratory measurement on the low frequency (50 Hz to 10 kHz) screening. The screening effectiveness for signalling cables of traditional structure and that of improved design has been compared by real scale site tests. For this purposes the cables of both constructions have been installed along identical routes in the switchyard of an open air 220kV/120kV/20kV substation. The interference levels transferred into the common mode loop of the tested cables has been measured by the following EMI sources: • current injection into the earthing grid at 50 Hz • switching of a bus-bar by disconnector • injection of damped oscillatory wave (1 MHz) • injection of electrical fast transient/ burst (5/50 ns). The results of tests and the conclusions on the shielding performance of the improved sheath structures are described.

articleTitle: Microwave Field-to-Wire Coupling Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Knowledge of antenna receiving properties of wires and cables is essential in the analysis of susceptibility of electronic systems to microwave radiation. This paper presents measurements of receiving parameters for basic wire geometries. Directional properties of realized gain, receiving cross section and of effective antenna length for the wires are presented. The impact of measured directivity effects of the order of 15 dB on radiated susceptibility testing in anechoic and mode-stirred chambers is discussed.

articleTitle: The Influence of Shield Inhomogeneities on the Complex Transfer-Impedances and -Admittances of Shielded Multiconductor Cables
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The determination of the complex transfer impedances and transfer admittances of shielded multiconductor cables is the prerequisite for calculating disturbing currents on the inner wires of the cable. This paper shows a measurement procedure based on the improved        triaxial measurement set-ups using multiconductor transmission line theory for evaluation. With this method of evaluation it is possible to determine individual transfer impedances and admittances for each inner conductor of a shielded multiconductor cable over a broad frequency range also in the case of a shield inhomogeneity.

articleTitle: Fast EMC Analysis for Printed Circuit Boards using an Equivalent-Wire Method of Moments
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The EMC analysis of printed circuit boards with the method of moments combined with an equivalent wire model offers the advantages of small modeling effort and short computation time. Being a full-wave method, it includes all electromagnetic phenomena encountered in modem printed circuit boards, e.g. transmission line effects, reflection, and mutual trace coupling, for arbitrary complex nets. This simplifying approach which has been recently used for the prediction of radiated emissions is further investigated giving validity ranges and error estimations. An extension for the treatment of large trace widths and the accurate computation of radiated fields using appropriate Green’s functions, including vertical currents within the PCB substrate is presented. Validation by more rigorous analysis examples indicates the broad range of practical application.

articleTitle: Microwave Radiation of Lightning Discharge
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper the results of the observations of impulse microwave radiation (MWR) of lightning discharge with the help of the radiometer at the wave length of 8 millimeters with the high time of resolution are presented. Experimental results are compared with the data of the evaluation calculations and with the data from the literature, extrapolated on the millimeter range. The conclusion is made that the registered signals are caused by the current impulses, emerging in the storm cloud and in the channel on the stages of stepped leader and return stroke.

articleTitle: Changes in Plasma Membrane Organization Induced by Exposure to ELF and to Amplitude Modulated Radiofrequencies
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Human B cells exposure for 72 hrs to extremely low electromagnetic field (ELF) or amplitude modulated radiofrequency resulted in a dramatic change of the plasma membrane morphology. Together with the change in morphology we could detect a different actin distribution and natural killer (NK) activity.

articleTitle: Study of Propagation Constant for a Single Buried Wire in a Lossy Ground
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The behavior of the propagation constant of current on a buried isolated wire in a lossy ground is studied and depicted. A numerical resolution method, Muller’s method, is used to solve the exact expression of the modal equation in the frequency domain. Results are given for a typical structure of buried cable, in a large range of frequencies from 1 Hz to 1 GHz, with a good stability. The determination of the propagation constant of the line allows us to give the behavior of the impedance and the admittance of the line. Some differences with approximations for very low frequencies already given by some scientists appear. Then we propose an approximated expression for the propagation constant, which provides good results for the high frequencies.

articleTitle: The Performances of Chokes with Toroidal Ferrite Cores for Power EMI-Filters
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The authors are presenting an original complex eletrical scheme for the chokes with ferrite cores. Using this scheme, the inductive and capacitive behaviours of the impedance of the choke are explained for a wide frequency range. Also, the paper offers the possibility of design a power EMI-filter, based on the exact knowing of the proper behaviour of the choke with ferrite core.

articleTitle: A New Approach for Automotive Electromagnetic Compatibility Tests in Production
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a new method for testing electromagnetic compatibility of cars in a production environment. This one used a statistic approach instead of a numerical approach. As electronic becomes more and more important in vehicles, electromagnetic compatibility is yet very important within the automotive industry. For testing the immunity, the manufacturers used the traditional technique : the final representative car are tested for radiated susceptibility in a semi-anechoic EMC chamber, according the normalisation; This technique takes a long time and it is not possible to test a large variety of vehicles in production. So the idea is to test the cars earlier in the cycle of production and to test all the vehicles in the manufacture ( and not in a specific area ). Two approaches can be applied. First, a numerical approach can be used. The different types of cars and components in cars are modelled and the variation in the development can be taken in account to see the compatibility effect. The second approach is a statistical approach. The susceptibility of cars can be measured on a large panel of representative cars, and so the probability of dysfunction can be evaluated. The results are compared with the statistics. The risk is then evaluated.

articleTitle: Superposition Properties of Radiated Emission from Large Telecommunication Equipment
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is useful to examine superposition properties of radiated emissions from telecommunication equipment planing the emission distributions. In this paper, superposition properties of emission for telecommunication equipment, which consists with several frames are examined. From the experimental results, it is found that the superposition properties of emissions are given as a function of power summation of each emission level of the frames.

articleTitle: Radiation Directivity of a Buried Leaky Coaxial Cable in a Guided Radar System
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The theoretical and experimental investigations of the radiation directivity of the buried leaky coaxial cable (LCC) are presented. The theoretical model of two coupling waveguides, external of which consists sub-soil medium, is introduced to describe interactions of two modes, external and internal which determine the working characteristics of such a leaky coaxial cable. The theoretical analysis shows, that the main parameters affecting the performance of such a guided radar system are the attenuation, which limits the longitudinal range of LCC, and coupling, which determines the overall sensitivity and field pattern of radar system. The coupling coefficients depend on the internal and external parameters of LCC and sub-soil medium. Attenuation is relatively easy to measure by simple insertion loss techniques. Coupling is the measure of the signal accessibility at a given radial distance outside the cable and, being very dependent on the particular installation and environmental aspects. The vertical and the horizontal distribution of radiation along the cable are examined experimentally by use of the loop of the LCC buried at the depth ΙΟ1 5 cm. The electric field intensity distribution both along and accross the cable at the height ~0.8 m above the ground is measured. The comparison between experimental data and theoretical prediction of radiation directivity of LCC for guided radar system is presented.

articleTitle: Characterisation of Emission from Discontinuites and Interconnects in Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes the characterisation of discontinuities and interconnects commonly encountered in fast clock rate printed circuit boards. The approach is to use a full-field numerical simulation technique based on the TLM method. This provides a complete description of the problem in the time-domain from which various parameters such as the standing wave ratio (VSWR) and S - parameters can be obtained. Radiation field and current flows are also directly obtained over a wide frequency range. Representative examples from typical circuit features such as gaps, via holes and bridges are presented to help designers to assess the impact of design choices on electromagnetic emissions.

articleTitle: Fine Structure of MF Variations (0-10 Hz) Onboard DC Electrified Trains
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Biological experiments showed that, differently from ionizing radiation and most chemical factors, the effect of low-frequency magnetic fields (MF) appears to be highly non-linear, as indicated by the possible concern of intensity and frequency "windows", resonance-like phenomena, intermittence, transients and MF polarization. We present results of a magnetic survey performed during 1997-98 in Russia onboard DC trains. Studying the fine structure of transport-associated MF, we emphasize the importance of MF exposure parameters other than the customary considered time-weighted average field strength. Specifically, we consider the complex-frequency characteristics of these fields, including pulses, intermittent components, polarization and the sources of these potentially hazardous MF features. To measure magnetic fields we used a wave-form capture system (torsion-type magnetometer) developed by SPbFIZMIRAN (Russia). This computer-based device, with sampling rate up to 200 Hz, allows to capture a field profile and to characterize field amplitudes over time and frequency.

articleTitle: 3-D Analysis of EMI Reduction by the Image Planes of Finite Size
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The use of image planes is an effective method to reduce the radiated emissions from a printed circuit board(PCB). This paper deals with the influence of image planes on the radiation from PCB. The shielding performance of two layers of image planes of finite width and length is analyzed by the method of moments based on the triangular surface patch model. It is demonstrated that proper triangulation should be made so as to take two basis functions in the boundary triangles of the surface.

articleTitle: Immunity of Operational Amplifiers against HF and High Amplitude Pulse Interferences
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic interferences (EMI) entering various terminals of operational amplifiers (OpAmps) can cause significant distortion of the amplifier output voltage. This paper describes the results of investigation of few types of OpAmps manufactured in different technologies and subjected to the influence of harmonic out-of-band and hf pulse interferences. Input terminals of OpAmp, its supply lines and adopted working circuits together with selected outer passive components were taken into account in the analysis.

articleTitle: Induced Currents on Metallic Cabinet Due to the Lightning Stroke Radiated Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) model for the lightning protection system of a building is presented. This model makes possible to analize the electromagnetic environment inside the building during direct or nearby lightning strike and to solve complex and practical EMC problems such as the coupling of the field generated by the LPS (during a direct or nearby lightning strike) with metallic boxes containing large mainframes or telecommunication apparata. A matrix solution of the whole set of equations describing the LPS and the boxes allows one to predict the current distribution in the LPS downconductors and the induced voltages and currents on the metallic surfaces of the boxes. Results are given in frequency and time domain for direct and nearby lightning strike and for different position and grounding of the cabinets inside the LPS volume.

articleTitle: Determination of Semi-Anechoic-Chamber Performance: Critical Evaluation and a Suggestion for Improvement
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The new EMC-Standards in Europe prescribe good agreement between measured and analytical calculated NSA for EMC emission test environments. However, those analytically calculated values are inaccurate and include approximations. This may lead to deviations of measured and calculated NSA of more than 4 dB even at an ideal open area test site. In this paper a method for the exact determination of the chamber performance is introduced. The measured SA-values are not normalized to NSA, but directly compared to numerical calculations. The accuracy of the numerical calculation is verified and the results are compared to the values given in the standards. The investigations are concentrated on different EMC antenna types.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Fields within Buildings Caused by Common-Mode Currents on Telecommunication Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the immediate future, many telecommunication operators plan to offer very high bitrate digital data connections to their customers through ordinary copper telephone lines. As such use of the lines was not conceived of when they were installed, the EMI-problems caused by such new services on the lines have to be considered. It is likely that the most serious EMI-problems could occur in receivers in the medium- and shortwave ranges due to common-mode current radiation. Therefore, electromagnetic fields in multi-storey buildings due to common-mode currents on telecommunication lines are analysed rigorously by means of an integral equation approach. The main numerical results, such as the qualitative behaviour of the field levels within the building, are compared with measurements done within a multi-storey house of slightly different dimensions. In this presentation the frequency range of interest is chosen to be 10 kHz - 30 MHz and so the very near field is of primary interest. To compare the theoretical results with experimental data, the induced voltage in simple probe antennas is found to be a useful quantity to be considered in the theoretical model. From this voltage, with the application of the calibration factor of these antennas, the average field strength at the antenna position is calculated and compared with that from the measurements. We found good agreement in the qualitative behaviour of the field levels. The E-field level is nearly constant within the building while the H-field level decreases with increasing distance from the source. Of course, there are many resonances at higher frequencies. The highest field levels are observed at about 1 MHz if the lines are fed with a constant-voltage source.

articleTitle: About Disturbances in Power Systems at the Transients Due to Switching Operations of Multiple Capacitor Banks
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The study presents the main disturbances, generated by the transitory phenomena at the commutation of simple and multiple capacitor banks. The same are presented electromagnetic stresses modelling features at the commutation of capacitor banks as part of the National Electical Energetic System. Successfully used for the compensation of wattles-inductive energy, capacitor banks are characterized during connecting and reenergize of electric arc by the powerful current shocks, which produces dynamic, thermal stresses and electrical wear extremely pernicious for the commutation equipment for the banks themselves and for electrical network, thus possible serious disturbances in the Power Systems may occur. At the disconnection of simple capacitor banks but more especially at the disconnection of multiplecapacitor banks may appear an important commutation overvoltage, which in certain occasions may become very dangerous for the apparatus-network assembly and sometimes even for the environment. This stress evaluation is based on adequate numerical programs concerning certain equipment and capacitor banks as part of the Power Systems. The final part of this study contains proposals and recommendations for construction, function, operation of the assembly capacitor banks-circuit breaker-network, to limit the level of stress and to rise the security in function.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility between Single Wire Earth Return Lines and Adjacent Telecommunication Systems in South African Conditions
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The increasing use of SWER (single wire earth return) networks in South Africa has led Eskom to review existing methods for determining separation between SWER systems and telephone lines. About 762 km of SWER exists in South Africa at present, and a further 926 km is planned to be built within the next 5 years. Important parameters in determining such separations are the voltage telephone form factor (TFF) and equivalent disturbing current (EDC) of the SWER systems. Although some publications (notably the Australian SWER standards) specify such levels, it was felt necessary to do surveys of this type of distortion in existing lightly loaded SWER networks. The resulting measured values of voltage TFF agree well-with the Australian levels, but at times exceed them; the measured values of EDC in certain light load conditions differ from the predicted values, being at times much lower. In addition, it is shown that (for specific soil conditions) the measured mutual impedances at voiceband frequencies generally agree closely with those predicted by the theory of Klewe. The measured 50 Hz mutual impedances tend to be higher than those predicted.

articleTitle: Comparison of Electromagnetic Fields Produced from Overhead Power Transmission Lines to Distribution Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The interest about the possible influence of low-frequency electromagnetic fields on human health, does not loose in its actuality. Since the Vancouver case in 1989 up till widely discussed disturbances in one German family in 1997, the public and professional interest is increasing. The importance of investigation in this area is clear from the fact that organizations involved only with the technical side of the issue are spending great amount of money (EPRI $50 million, U.S. DoE $65 million, etc.)[1]. Modeling and managing of low-frequency electromagnetic fields requires verification of theory with actual measurements. Measurements of electric and magnetic fields under overhead transmission and distribution lines are presented in this paper. These measured values are compared with theoretical calculated results. Also, the single axis waveform measurements of the magnetic field is presented together with the frequency spectrum analyse. The magnetic fields near distribution lines may be comparable and richer in harmonics to those produced by transmission lines.

articleTitle: Finite Length Line Model for the Analysis of Electro-Manetic Processes with Regard to Radiation
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A mathematical model of a horizontal line of finite length for calculating fast transient processes in the time domain is proposed. The mathematical model of the line is based on a finite difference approximation of the integro-differential equations, which are more general then the traditionally telegraphic equations. The well-known method of dividing the line in a number of segments with lumped elements is used. The originally is that mutual interaction between the different segments are taken into account. As the equivalent circuits are convenient mathematical models for calculations electromagnetic processes in the lines the use of equivalent circuits represents an advantage. It is shown that only for segments situated at the line ends the mutual interaction must be considered. This model takes in an approximative way into account the phenomenon of electromagnetic energy radiation. The line model can be combined with load models, including non-linear devices.

articleTitle: Statistical Process Control in an E3 Test Laboratory
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Measurement system variability in a test laboratory can be a source of discomfort for the test engineer. The use of Statistical Process Control (SPC) methods to gage and track the variability of system measurements can provide confidence in the repeatability of the system setup, and in the data it produces. The use of SPC in an EMC Lab, especially for frequency domain measurements, requires decisions to limit the quantity of the data to avoid information overload. To accomplish this careful selection of the measurement methods is essential.

articleTitle: An Asymptotic Approach for the Calculation of Electromagnetic Field Coupling to Long Terminated Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we present and validate an analytical expression for the induced current on a long terminated line, under the thin wire approximation. The coefficients of the analytical expression are determined using a procedure based on the knowledge of the exact solutions for a short line. The length of the short line is independent of the original line length, and therefore the method is very efficient when considering the electromagnetic coupling to very long lines.

articleTitle: Robin Boundary Condition Iteration: A Method for Solving Scattering Problems in EMC Applications
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper an iterative FEM method is proposed for the solution of scattering problems in EMC applications. A fictitious truncation boundary is introduced near the scatterer, on which a suitable Robin (mixed) boundary condition is first guessed and then iteratively improved making use of the free-space Green’s function. Examples are given in order to show the feasibility of the method in the solution of typical EMC problems.

articleTitle: The Effect of Noise on the Behaviour of Neuronal Cells Exposed to Pulsed Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work the response of a theoretical model of neuronal cells is analyzed for electromagnetic (EM) fields used for Mobile Telecommunication Equipments (MTE). In particular the theoretical model describing the behaviour of a neuronal cell is firstly presented together with the characterization of the EM signals used in most MTE. Then particular attention is devoted to the introduction of a noise source into the model. Two different types of noise sources are considered: the first which takes into account the noise accompanying the EM signal incident on the cell and the second which models the noise derived from the activity of the cell membrane. Both type of noise sources are modelled as white gaussian noise. The results show that the presence of noise alter significantly (especially in one case) the response of the neuronal model to the EM exposure.

articleTitle: EM Susceptibility of PCB Inside Equipment Housing
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a method of evaluating the susceptibility of printed circuits inside the equipment housing to incoming electromagnetic waves through an aperture on the housing wall. The field distribution inside the housing and, also, the current induced in a transmission line on a PCB placed inside the housing were analyzed by the transmission-line modeling method. Results of the analysis showed a good agreement with the results of measurement. Also, it is found that the susceptibility of the PCB shows peaks at some frequencies that depend almost solely on the structure of the housing and the aperture and, therefore, can be estimated at the time of equipment design.

articleTitle: Calculation of Current Distribution in the Human Body around 765 kV Transmission Lines of Korea
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Safety related to field exposure for the personnel in substation is of importance. For complicated and time-consuming three-dimensional calculation of induced current on human body, this paper proposes an effective numerical calculation method based on CSM and SCM. The proposed method can be adopted in the condition of nonuniform electric field around transmission lines. And, this method is applied to 765 kV transmission lines in Korea.

articleTitle: Linear-Geometry Electric-Field Probe for DC Corona Measurements and Application to Field Distribution in Wire-to-Plane Geometry
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new measurement of current density and field with biased probe, during the positive corona discharge, is developed in this paper. In this work, we have elucidated the phenomena of probe end-effects when it is biased. Our prototype of the probe, without endeffects, has been adapted to a linear geometry. The probe functions were verified and thus the actual theoretical model, which simulates the biased probe by the coplanar planes system, is verified. The measured field increase linearly with the corona voltage. The current density and the electric field decrease as we move away from the centre of plane. Moreover, we used this probe to measure the electric field at plane as function of the distance between the wire and the plane.

articleTitle: Interaction of Wired it Networks and Mobile Telecommunication Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The increasing density of mobile telecommunication systems together with current trends in electronic device technology may result in an increased risk of EMC problems between wired IT networks and mobile communication systems. Simulations of the coupling between wired networks and mobile sources using a moment method code show that common-mode currents can be the dominant source of EMI if mode conversion mechanisms are present in the system. A technique for predicting the EMI caused by common-mode currents is presented.

articleTitle: Field Strength Prediction in Urban Area: A Ray-Tracing Algorithm
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A general formulation of a ray-tracing algorithm is presented, which permits the evaluation of field propagation in non regular urban area, as typical of Italian towns. The field strength in any point is calculated, providing a useful tool in order to evaluate interference levels or planning mobile communication systems. The simulation program takes into account the tree canopies effects on the path loss, assuming an additional attenuation for the rays propagating through canopies. The comparison with measurements shows a good agreement, so confirming the validity of the model.

articleTitle: Chaotic Dynamics in Lossy Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A time domain open loop representation of a lossy line is used for the study of bifurcations and chaotic dynamics, when the line is terminated on nonlinear active resistors. In particular, bifurcation diagrams are evaluated for different levels of losses along the line. The qualitative and quantitative behaviours of the dynamics are shown to be dependent on the losses. The analysis is paralleled by the lossless case, and some similarities as well as differences are shown.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of Perforated Magnetostatic Enclosures
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The diffusional process of the magnetic field inside a high-μ enclosure with openings is carefully investigated. A simple formula, representing the altered shielding factor when the shell reluctance is increased by the holes, is given. The technique exploits the theory of mixtures to take into account the effect of a given number of dispersed holes. As a subsidiary application, the residual field penetrated into the inner region directly from the holes has been assessed, after employing a numerical method to evaluate the overall impairment.

articleTitle: Analysis and Estimation of Radiated Emissions of Distribution Boxes in the Access Area of Telecommunication Networks
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: New developments in transmission technology (e.g. ADSL, VDSL) offer the potential of highspeed digital transmission over existing copper-wire access networks. Since these networks were not originally designed for carrying high frequencies, an examination of the possible interfering effects is necessary. This paper treats the problem of radiated emissions from distribution boxes at the crossconnection points. The cause of these emissions is analysed by numerical simulations. Based on this work, a method is proposed to estimate the emission of complex systems. Reduction effects which occur at a large number of connections are also considered. The method is demonstrated by means of an example.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Non-Gaussian Probability Density of Signals and Interferences
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In work it is offered the resulting probability density of set of signal (interference) parameters to describe through a mixture of private probability densities. For definition of unknown parameters of private probability densities it is offered to use method of maximal likelihood. Report receives and resolves the maximal likelihood equations for practically important case when the private probability densities of moments of signal arrivals are subject to Gaussian law.

articleTitle: Dosimetry and Exposure Experiments for Extremely Low Frequency High-Tension Electric Field Therapy
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The high-tension electric field therapy (EF Therapy) has been long used in Japan. This EL Therapy uses extremely low frequency ( mainly 50Hz or 60Hz ) electric fields. This paper describes the dosimetry for EL Therapy and introduces the results of the exposure experiments of persons in EL Therapy.

articleTitle: Modelling and Experimental Activity About the Coupling of ESD Through the Grounding System
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we report some results dealing with our investigation about the role played by the grounding system in the coupling between an electrostatic discharge (ESD) event and a possible victim component or system. This investigation has been made with two connected scientific activities. The numerical modelling and simulation of the system (ESD + grounding + victim) has been made by means of a suitable application of the Finite-Difference in Time Domain (FDTD) technique. This numerical technique has been studied in particular in order to well simulate the ESD source in complex geometries, where there are interconnection conductors, that pass through the boundary of the investigated region and reach far grounding systems. The experimental activity has been carried out in order either to check the numerical procedure or to measure the interferences conducted via the grounding system to possible susceptible electronic devices. The practical problems encountered and solved during this experimental activity are presented and discussed in the paper. Preliminary results applied to radial or meshed grounding systems seems to prove the effectiveness and the accuracy of the numerical modelling technique proposed. Finally some quantitative and qualitative considerations about the level of the interference produced and of the coupling degree vs. the position of the ESD and the configuration of the grounding system are reported.

articleTitle: An Improved Model for Studying Dry Band Arcing on All Dielectric Self Supporting Fiber Optic Cable Located near High Voltage Power Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In recent years it has become common for utilities to locate optical fiber communications systems on their transmission lines. The need for internal utility communications and the desire for revenue from leased fibers have driven this activity. Several cable options exist. The first is optical ground wires (OPGW) in which the fibers are installed at the center of ground wires normally used for lightning protection. The second (WRAP) is an all dielectric cable which is wrapped around phase conductors on lower voltage lines or ground wires on higher voltage lines. The third is all dielectric self supporting (ADSS) cable which is mounted below the phase conductors.

articleTitle: EMC Analysis of the Satellite Communication Equipment Under Influence of a Multitude of Interference
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper proposes a new approach for EMC analysis of communications systems which are affected by a “multitude” of the interference. It happens, when the systems are affected by interference sources of different physical nature (spurious radiation from disturbing equipment, man-made noise from switching stage and power supplies, etc). The latter case is named here after as a case of “multitude” of interference and in the paper is considered an analytical treatment for EMC analysis in the mentioned conditions.

articleTitle: Time Domain Characterization of a System by using CW Measurement Results Without Phase Information
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In EMC tests, systems are usually described by their frequency response(FR). However, only using the magnitude of the FR, a system cannot be described completely, because the phase information is unknown. This paper discusses the method of estimating the time domain characteristic (for example, the pulse response) of a system from the magnitude of FR without knowing the phase information. A minimal phase system is used to approximate the real system. The Hilbert transform is first used to relate magnitude to phase of the FR, then a discrete transfer function model is estimated to describe the system. Examples are given to show the applications of this method in system modeling, signal reconstruction and time domain response prediction.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Harmonics in Nonlinear Electric Power Networks Including the Elements with Frequency Dependent Parameters
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method of analysis of harmonics in electric power networks permitting the taking into account nonlinear and frequency properties of elements of electric power networks is considered. The method uses a time domain and does not impose limitations on the form of nonlinear and frequency characteristics of elements. The result of calculating by this method can be not only harmonics spectra, but also real time dependences of currents and voltages on the devices of a network. The method offers an effective solution to the problems of electromagnetic compatibility in the field of power engineering with a minimum number of assumptions. The processes in electric power networks of a substation of an arc furnace using the capacitor battery for compensation of reactive power are considered.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Stability and Numerical Dispersion of the FDTD Method with “Sliding Window” for Non Linear Problems
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The wave equation in discretised form using finite differences has different properties as compared with the true differential form. The issues of stability and numerical dispersion are thoroughly investigated here, for exact formulation as well as for slowly varying envelope approximation. Use of ”sliding computational window” decreases computational complexity but changes properties of discretised equations.

articleTitle: A Classification Scheme for EMI Failure in Opamp Circuits
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we consider the effects of failures induced from EMI on integrated operational amplifiers built with different technologies. In particular, we describe some typical shapes of the mean value output voltage found in opamps subjected to EMI conveyed to their inputs and we propose a classification method to define useful parameters both to foresee the opamps behavior with respect to these types of failure and to suggest design guidelines.

articleTitle: Complex Permittivity Measurement of Foam Materials using a One-Port Network Analyser Measurement
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method of complex permittivity extraction is proposed based on a single one-port vector sample measurement for non-magnetic media applicable to carbon doped foams for example. The reflection data is numerically processed to allow for non-coincidence of the measurement and calibration plane and is suitable for both transmission line and waveguide measurement schemes. Extraction of the parameters is based on a genetic algorithm optimiser with a suitable error function as the solution is nonanalytic and the error surface is not unconditionally suitable for a simple gradient technique. Unlike descent methods the genetic algorithm handles local minima in an efficient manner.

articleTitle: Deviations in Residual Inhomogeneity of Electromagnetic Fields for Immunity Tests by Isotropic or Vector Measuring Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We consider the influence of different measurement equipment and procedures on the quality of electromagnetic standard fields for immunity tests. For such tests against electromagnetic fields different kinds of field generators are established according to international standards, i.e. antennas in semi anechoic chambers, (G)TEM-cells etc. Even following strictly the test requirements and procedures of (European) standards gives no guarantee that test results are the same in all test laboratories. Technical reasons for this phenomenon are mainly insufficient absorption of scattered electromagnetic fields in field generators (anecoic chamber or (G)TEM-cell), the type of measuring equipment, and the test object. We found field variations of up to 3 dB, in extreme cases (chamber resonances) more than 10 dB.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multiconductor Transmission Lines Networks: State-Variable Characterization of Junctions and Terminations
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper proposes a general method for the transient analysis of lossy multiconductor transmission line (MTL) networks having arbitrary junctions. The propagation of voltages and currents along the TL is analyzed by the FDTD algorithm. This approach is combined with a state-variable characterization of the junctions. Several numerical examples and comparisons are given and show the reliability of the resulting hybrid method.

articleTitle: Inverter-Fed Induction Motor Drive Model for Determining the Stray Current Disturbances
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The models of a PWM voltage inverter-fed induction motor drive for the common and differential current modes are presented. Models of the feeding cable with lumped or distributed parameters are incorporated in both representations of the drive system. The frequency and transient responses represent the starting point for determining the parameters of the drive for high frequencies. The transfer functions of different models have been calculated and a lot of simulations and experiments done.

articleTitle: Numerical Representation of Cellular Phones: Procedure and Accuracy
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An automated tool for the representation of general objects in a discretized space is presented applied to cellular phones. The mesher provides also for the positioning of the phone to the head/phantom as requested by international standards. A complete automated procedure for the geometrical description of the cellular phone’s geometry is used and described. The computed electromagnetic field distribution and the radiation patterns are compared for a realistic model of the cellular phone and for an approximated model in order to highlight the differences.

articleTitle: Rectangular Coax with Axial Slit and with Rectangular or Circular Center Conductor
publicationTitle: EMC'98 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The analysis of rectangular coax with axial slit and with rectangular or circular center conductor is based on the equivalent electrodes method. The obtained values of characteristic impedance, resistance per unit line length and electric field distribution are presented and the influence of the slit is investigated.
